passages.text: Then Samuel took a flask of oil, poured it on Saul’s head, kissed him, and said, “Has not the LORD anointed you ruler over His inheritance?
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of God.
Saul was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin.
Samuel took a flask of oil.
Samuel poured the oil on Saul’s head.
Samuel kissed Saul.
Samuel said, “The LORD has anointed you.”
The LORD made you ruler over His inheritance.
God chose you to lead His people.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֨ח שְׁמוּאֵ֜ל אֶת־ פַּ֥ךְ הַשֶּׁ֛מֶן וַיִּצֹ֥ק עַל־ רֹאשׁ֖וֹ וַיִּשָּׁקֵ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הֲל֗וֹא כִּֽי־ מְשָׁחֲךָ֧ יְהוָ֛ה עַל־ נַחֲלָת֖וֹ לְנָגִֽיד׃

passages.text: When you leave me today, you will find two men at Rachel’s tomb in Zelzah on the border of Benjamin. They will say to you, ‘The donkeys you seek have been found, and now your father has stopped worrying about the donkeys and started worrying about you, asking, “What should I do about my son?” ’
passages.sermon:
Samuel spoke to Saul.
Samuel gave Saul a sign for that day.
Samuel said, “When you leave me today, you will meet two men.”
You will find these two men at Rachel’s tomb.
Rachel’s tomb is in Zelzah.
Zelzah is on the border of Benjamin.
The two men will speak to you.
They will say, ‘The donkeys you went to look for have been found.’
They will also say, ‘Now your father has stopped thinking about the donkeys.’
‘Your father is worried about you.’
‘He is asking, “What should I do about my son?”’
passages.original: בְּלֶכְתְּךָ֤ הַיּוֹם֙ מֵעִמָּדִ֔י וּמָצָאתָ֩ שְׁנֵ֨י אֲנָשִׁ֜ים עִם־ קְבֻרַ֥ת רָחֵ֛ל בִּגְב֥וּל בִּנְיָמִ֖ן בְּצֶלְצַ֑ח וְאָמְר֣וּ אֵלֶ֗יךָ נִמְצְא֤וּ הָאֲתֹנוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָלַ֣כְתָּ לְבַקֵּ֔שׁ וְהִנֵּ֨ה נָטַ֤שׁ אָבִ֙יךָ֙ אֶת־ דִּבְרֵ֣י הָאֲתֹנ֔וֹת וְדָאַ֤ג לָכֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מָ֥ה אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה לִבְנִֽי׃

passages.text: Then you will go on from there until you come to the Oak of Tabor. Three men going up to God at Bethel will meet you there, one carrying three young goats, another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a skin of wine.
passages.sermon:
You will leave this place and continue on your way.
You will come to the Oak of Tabor.
Three men will meet you there.
These men are going up to God at Bethel.
One man will carry three young goats.
Another man will carry three loaves of bread.
Another man will carry a skin of wine.
passages.original: וְחָלַפְתָּ֨ מִשָּׁ֜ם וָהָ֗לְאָה וּבָ֙אתָ֙ עַד־ אֵל֣וֹן תָּב֔וֹר וּמְצָא֤וּךָ שָּׁם֙ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים עֹלִ֥ים אֶל־ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בֵּֽית־ אֵ֑ל אֶחָ֞ד נֹשֵׂ֣א׀ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְדָיִ֗ים וְאֶחָד֙ נֹשֵׂ֗א שְׁלֹ֙שֶׁת֙ כִּכְּר֣וֹת לֶ֔חֶם וְאֶחָ֥ד נֹשֵׂ֖א נֵֽבֶל־ יָֽיִן׃

passages.text: They will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you will accept from their hands.
passages.sermon:
Three men will meet you at the Oak of Tabor.
They will greet you.
They will give you two loaves of bread.
You will take the bread from their hands.
passages.original: וְשָׁאֲל֥וּ לְךָ֖ לְשָׁל֑וֹם וְנָתְנ֤וּ לְךָ֙ שְׁתֵּי־ לֶ֔חֶם וְלָקַחְתָּ֖ מִיָּדָֽם׃

passages.text: After that you will come to Gibeah of God, where the Philistines have an outpost. As you approach the city, you will meet a group of prophets coming down from the high place, preceded by harps, tambourines, flutes, and lyres, and they will be prophesying.
passages.sermon:
You will go to Gibeah of God.
The Philistines have an outpost there.
You will approach the city.
You will meet a group of prophets.
These prophets are coming down from the high place.
Musicians go before them.
The musicians play harps, tambourines, flutes, and lyres.
The prophets are prophesying.
passages.original: אַ֣חַר כֵּ֗ן תָּבוֹא֙ גִּבְעַ֣ת הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־ שָׁ֖ם נְצִבֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וִיהִי֩ כְבֹאֲךָ֨ שָׁ֜ם הָעִ֗יר וּפָגַעְתָּ֞ חֶ֤בֶל נְבִיאִים֙ יֹרְדִ֣ים מֵֽהַבָּמָ֔ה וְלִפְנֵיהֶ֞ם נֵ֤בֶל וְתֹף֙ וְחָלִ֣יל וְכִנּ֔וֹר וְהֵ֖מָּה מִֽתְנַבְּאִֽים׃

passages.text: Then the Spirit of the LORD will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them; and you will be transformed into a different person.
passages.sermon: The Spirit of the LORD will come upon you with power.\r\nYou will prophesy with the group of prophets.\r\nGod will change you into a different person.
passages.original: וְצָלְחָ֤ה עָלֶ֙יךָ֙ ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה וְהִתְנַבִּ֖יתָ עִמָּ֑ם וְנֶהְפַּכְתָּ֖ לְאִ֥ישׁ אַחֵֽר׃

passages.text: When these signs have come, do as the occasion demands, for God is with you.
passages.sermon:
God chose Saul to be king.
God gave Saul special signs to confirm this.
When these signs happen to you, act as the situation requires.
God is with you.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּ֥י תְבֹאֶינָה הָאֹת֥וֹת הָאֵ֖לֶּה לָ֑ךְ עֲשֵׂ֤ה לְךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּמְצָ֣א יָדֶ֔ךָ כִּ֥י הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: And you shall go before me to Gilgal, and surely I will come to you to offer burnt offerings and to sacrifice peace offerings. Wait seven days until I come to you and show you what you are to do.”
passages.sermon:
Samuel spoke to Saul.
Samuel was a prophet of God.
Saul was chosen to be king.
Samuel said, “You will go down to Gilgal before me.
I will come to you at Gilgal.
I will offer burnt offerings there.
I will sacrifice peace offerings there.
You must wait seven days.
Wait until I come to you.
I will tell you what you must do.”
passages.original: וְיָרַדְתָּ֣ לְפָנַי֮ הַגִּלְגָּל֒ וְהִנֵּ֤ה אָֽנֹכִי֙ יֹרֵ֣ד אֵלֶ֔יךָ לְהַעֲל֣וֹת עֹל֔וֹת לִזְבֹּ֖חַ זִבְחֵ֣י שְׁלָמִ֑ים שִׁבְעַ֨ת יָמִ֤ים תּוֹחֵל֙ עַד־ בּוֹאִ֣י אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְהוֹדַעְתִּ֣י לְךָ֔ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: As Saul turned to leave Samuel, God changed Saul’s heart, and all the signs came to pass that day.
passages.sermon:
Saul was a man from the tribe of Benjamin.
Samuel was a prophet of God.
Saul turned to leave Samuel.
God changed Saul’s heart.
All the signs that Samuel had spoken came to pass that day.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֗ה כְּהַפְנֹת֤וֹ שִׁכְמוֹ֙ לָלֶ֙כֶת֙ מֵעִ֣ם שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַיַּהֲפָךְ־ ל֥וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים לֵ֣ב אַחֵ֑ר וַיָּבֹ֛אוּ כָּל־ הָאֹת֥וֹת הָאֵ֖לֶּה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃ס

passages.text: When Saul and his servant arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. Then the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied along with them.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the son of Kish.
Saul traveled with his servant.
They arrived at Gibeah.
A group of prophets came to meet Saul.
The Spirit of God came powerfully upon Saul.
Saul began to prophesy with the prophets.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ שָׁם֙ הַגִּבְעָ֔תָה וְהִנֵּ֥ה חֶֽבֶל־ נְבִאִ֖ים לִקְרָאת֑וֹ וַתִּצְלַ֤ח עָלָיו֙ ר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיִּתְנַבֵּ֖א בְּתוֹכָֽם׃

passages.text: All those who had formerly known Saul and saw him prophesying with the prophets asked one another, “What has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the son of Kish.
Many people had known Saul before this day.
These people saw Saul with the prophets.
They saw Saul prophesying with the prophets.
The people were surprised.
Each person asked his neighbor, “What has happened to the son of Kish?”
They also asked, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כָּל־ יֽוֹדְעוֹ֙ מֵאִתְּמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשׁ֔וֹם וַיִּרְא֕וּ וְהִנֵּ֥ה עִם־ נְבִאִ֖ים נִבָּ֑א וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הָעָ֜ם אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־ רֵעֵ֗הוּ מַה־ זֶּה֙ הָיָ֣ה לְבֶן־ קִ֔ישׁ הֲגַ֥ם שָׁא֖וּל בַּנְּבִיאִֽים׃

passages.text: Then a man who lived there replied, “And who is their father?” So the saying became a proverb: “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
passages.sermon:
A man who lived in Gibeah answered.
He said, “Who is their father?”
People began to use a saying.
They said, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַן אִ֥ישׁ מִשָּׁ֛ם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר וּמִ֣י אֲבִיהֶ֑ם עַל־ כֵּן֙ הָיְתָ֣ה לְמָשָׁ֔ל הֲגַ֥ם שָׁא֖וּל בַּנְּבִאִֽים׃

passages.text: And when Saul had finished prophesying, he went up to the high place.
passages.sermon: Saul finished prophesying.\r\nHe went up to the high place.
passages.original: וַיְכַל֙ מֵֽהִתְנַבּ֔וֹת וַיָּבֹ֖א הַבָּמָֽה׃

passages.text: Now Saul’s uncle asked him and his servant, “Where did you go?” “To look for the donkeys,” Saul replied. “When we saw they were not to be found, we went to Samuel.”
passages.sermon:
Saul had an uncle.
Saul’s uncle spoke to Saul and to Saul’s servant.
Saul’s uncle asked them a question.
He said, “Where did you go?”
Saul answered his uncle.
Saul said, “We went to look for the donkeys.”
Saul continued speaking.
He said, “We saw that the donkeys were not there.”
Saul said, “So we went to Samuel.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ דּ֨וֹד שָׁא֥וּל אֵלָ֛יו וְאֶֽל־ נַעֲר֖וֹ אָ֣ן הֲלַכְתֶּ֑ם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לְבַקֵּשׁ֙ אֶת־ הָ֣אֲתֹנ֔וֹת וַנִּרְאֶ֣ה כִי־ אַ֔יִן וַנָּב֖וֹא אֶל־ שְׁמוּאֵֽל׃

passages.text: “Tell me,” Saul’s uncle asked, “what did Samuel say to you?”
passages.sermon:
Saul had an uncle.
Saul’s uncle spoke to Saul.
Saul’s uncle asked Saul a question.
Saul’s uncle said, “Tell me.”
Saul’s uncle said, “What did Samuel say to you?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר דּ֣וֹד שָׁא֑וּל הַגִּֽידָה־ נָּ֣א לִ֔י מָֽה־ אָמַ֥ר לָכֶ֖ם שְׁמוּאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And Saul replied, “He assured us that the donkeys had been found.” But Saul did not tell his uncle what Samuel had said about the kingship.
passages.sermon:
Saul spoke to his uncle.
Saul said, “He told us the donkeys have been found.”
Saul did not tell his uncle about the matter of the kingship.
Samuel had spoken about the kingship.
Saul kept this part secret from his uncle.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל־ דּוֹד֔וֹ הַגֵּ֤ד הִגִּיד֙ לָ֔נוּ כִּ֥י נִמְצְא֖וּ הָאֲתֹנ֑וֹת וְאֶת־ דְּבַ֤ר הַמְּלוּכָה֙ לֹֽא־ הִגִּ֣יד ל֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֥ר שְׁמוּאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: After this, Samuel summoned the people to the LORD at Mizpah and said to the Israelites, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I brought Israel up out of Egypt, and I rescued you from the hands of the Egyptians and of all the kingdoms that oppressed you.’
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of God.
Samuel called all the people together at Mizpah.
Samuel gathered the Israelites before the LORD.
Samuel spoke to the Israelites.
Samuel said, “The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD says this:
‘I brought Israel out of Egypt.
I rescued you from the power of the Egyptians.
I saved you from all the kingdoms that oppressed you.’”
passages.original: וַיַּצְעֵ֤ק שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶת־ הָעָ֔ם אֶל־ יְהוָ֖ה הַמִּצְפָּֽה׃ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀ אֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל פ כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אָנֹכִ֛י הֶעֱלֵ֥יתִי אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וָאַצִּ֤יל אֶתְכֶם֙ מִיַּ֣ד מִצְרַ֔יִם וּמִיַּד֙ כָּל־ הַמַּמְלָכ֔וֹת הַלֹּחֲצִ֖ים אֶתְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: But today you have rejected your God, who saves you from all your troubles and afflictions, and you have said to Him, ‘No, set a king over us.’ Now therefore present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and clans.”
passages.sermon:
Samuel spoke to the Israelites.
Samuel said, “Today you have rejected your God.
God saves you from all your troubles.
God saves you from all your afflictions.
But you said to God, ‘Set a king over us.’
Now stand before the LORD.
Stand by your tribes.
Stand by your clans.”
passages.original: וְאַתֶּ֨ם הַיּ֜וֹם מְאַסְתֶּ֣ם אֶת־ אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁר־ ה֣וּא מוֹשִׁ֣יעַ לָכֶם֮ מִכָּל־ רָעוֹתֵיכֶ֣ם וְצָרֹֽתֵיכֶם֒ וַתֹּ֣אמְרוּ ל֔וֹ כִּי־ מֶ֖לֶךְ תָּשִׂ֣ים עָלֵ֑ינוּ וְעַתָּ֗ה הִֽתְיַצְּבוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לְשִׁבְטֵיכֶ֖ם וּלְאַלְפֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Thus Samuel had all the tribes of Israel come forward, and the tribe of Benjamin was selected.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet and leader of Israel.
Samuel called all the tribes of Israel to come forward.
The people of each tribe stood before him.
Samuel selected one tribe from among them.
The tribe of Benjamin was chosen.
passages.original: וַיַּקְרֵ֣ב שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת כָּל־ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּלָּכֵ֖ד שֵׁ֥בֶט בִּנְיָמִֽן׃

passages.text: Then he had the tribe of Benjamin come forward by its clans, and the clan of Matri was selected. Finally, Saul son of Kish was selected. But when they looked for him, they could not find him.
passages.sermon:
Samuel led the tribe of Benjamin to come forward by their clans.
He selected the clan of Matri from among them.
He then selected Saul, the son of Kish, from the clan of Matri.
They searched for Saul.
They could not find him.
passages.original: וַיַּקְרֵ֞ב אֶת־ שֵׁ֤בֶט בִּנְיָמִן֙ לְמִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ וַתִּלָּכֵ֖ד מִשְׁפַּ֣חַת הַמַּטְרִ֑י וַיִּלָּכֵד֙ שָׁא֣וּל בֶּן־ קִ֔ישׁ וַיְבַקְשֻׁ֖הוּ וְלֹ֥א נִמְצָֽא׃

passages.text: So again they inquired of the LORD, “Has the man come here yet?” And the LORD replied, “Behold, he has hidden himself among the baggage.”
passages.sermon:
The people could not find Saul.
They asked the LORD again.
They said, “Has the man come here yet?”
The LORD answered them.
The LORD said, “He is hiding.”
The LORD said, “He is among the baggage.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁאֲלוּ־ עוֹד֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה הֲבָ֥א ע֖וֹד הֲלֹ֣ם אִ֑ישׁס וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה הִנֵּה־ ה֥וּא נֶחְבָּ֖א אֶל־ הַכֵּלִֽים׃

passages.text: So they ran and brought Saul, and when he stood among the people, he was a head taller than any of the others.
passages.sermon:
The people ran quickly.
They brought Saul out from where he was hiding.
Saul stood among all the people.
Saul was taller than everyone else.
He was a head taller than any other person there.
passages.original: וַיָּרֻ֙צוּ֙ וַיִּקָּחֻ֣הוּ מִשָּׁ֔ם וַיִּתְיַצֵּ֖ב בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעָ֑ם וַיִּגְבַּהּ֙ מִכָּל־ הָעָ֔ם מִשִּׁכְמ֖וֹ וָמָֽעְלָה׃

passages.text: Samuel said to all the people, “Do you see the one the LORD has chosen? There is no one like him among all the people.” And all the people shouted, “Long live the king!”
passages.sermon:
Samuel spoke to all the people.
Samuel said, "Look at the man the LORD has chosen."
The LORD chose this man to be king.
There is no one like him among all the people.
All the people shouted together.
They said, "Long live the king!"
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֜ל אֶל־ כָּל־ הָעָ֗ם הַרְּאִיתֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּֽחַר־ בּ֣וֹ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין כָּמֹ֖הוּ בְּכָל־ הָעָ֑ם וַיָּרִ֧עוּ כָל־ הָעָ֛ם וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ יְחִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃פ

passages.text: Then Samuel explained to the people the rights of kingship. He wrote them on a scroll and laid it up before the LORD. And Samuel sent all the people away, each to his own home.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet and leader of Israel.
Samuel spoke to the people.
He explained the rights and duties of kingship.
He wrote these rules in a book.
He placed the book before the LORD.
Samuel sent all the people away.
Each person went to his own home.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר שְׁמוּאֵ֜ל אֶל־ הָעָ֗ם אֵ֚ת מִשְׁפַּ֣ט הַמְּלֻכָ֔ה וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב בַּסֵּ֔פֶר וַיַּנַּ֖ח לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיְשַׁלַּ֧ח שְׁמוּאֵ֛ל אֶת־ כָּל־ הָעָ֖ם אִ֥ישׁ לְבֵיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Saul also went to his home in Gibeah, and the men of valor whose hearts God had touched went with him.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the man God chose to be king.
Saul went to his home in Gibeah.
Some men were brave and strong.
God touched the hearts of these men.
These men of valor went with Saul.
passages.original: וְגַ֨ם־ שָׁא֔וּל הָלַ֥ךְ לְבֵית֖וֹ גִּבְעָ֑תָה וַיֵּלְכ֣וּ עִמּ֔וֹ הַחַ֕יִל אֲשֶׁר־ נָגַ֥ע אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּלִבָּֽם׃

passages.text: But some worthless men said, “How can this man save us?” So they despised him and brought him no gifts; but Saul remained silent about it.
passages.sermon:
Some men in Israel were worthless.
These men did not respect God or others.
They saw Saul, who was chosen as king.
They said, “How can this man save us?”
They despised Saul.
They did not bring Saul any gifts.
Saul heard their words.
Saul remained silent.
passages.original: וּבְנֵ֧י בְלִיַּ֣עַל אָמְר֗וּ מַה־ יֹּשִׁעֵ֙נוּ֙ זֶ֔ה וַיִּבְזֻ֕הוּ וְלֹֽא־ הֵבִ֥יאוּ ל֖וֹ מִנְחָ֑ה וַיְהִ֖י כְּמַחֲרִֽישׁ׃פ
